scenes.text: 5 realistic habits that cut $800 a month immediately

script.caption:
You don't have to stop living your life to save $800 a month. You just have to stop spending on autopilot.

1. Cook 4 dinners a week at home (~$300/mo)
2. Pack lunch 3 days a week (~$180/mo)
3. Wait 48 hours before any online order (~$180/mo)
4. Buy store brands (~$80/mo)
5. Cancel the subscriptions you forgot about (~$60/mo)

Want saving to feel fun for once? Link in bio.

scenes.text: 4 realistic habits that cut $400 a month immediately

script.caption:
$400 a month is $4,800 a year, and none of this is hard.

1. Shop from a list, no extras (~$140/mo)
2. One less takeout order a week (~$120/mo)
3. Coffee at home on weekdays (~$100/mo)
4. A cheaper phone plan (~$40/mo)

The app we use to track it is in our bio.

scenes.text: 6 realistic habits that cut $600 a month immediately

script.caption:

1. Meal prep on Sundays (~$200/mo)
2. Transit pass instead of rideshares (~$120/mo)
3. Buy used before you buy new (~$110/mo)
4. Two no-spend weekends a month (~$100/mo)
5. Walk anything under 20 minutes (~$40/mo)
6. Share streaming plans (~$30/mo)

scenes.text: Best saving tip I ever got: the night before payday, move whatever's left into savings. $5 or $500.

script.caption:
If it's still sitting there when your new paycheque lands, it feels like extra money. It isn't.

Move it out the night before and you start every pay period with only what you actually earned.

Try it for your next 3 paydays.

scenes.text: Quickest way to blow $5,000 in a year? Spend $13.70 a day on coffee and snacks.

script.caption:
$13.70 doesn't feel like much. Do it every day for a year and it's $5,000.

You don't have to quit. Cut it in half and that's $2,500 back.
